children: New Delhi, Nov. 1 -- Shares of Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL), Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL) will remain in focus on Monday following the central government's latest decision on fuel taxation.

The central government, on Saturday, October 31, raised windfall gains tax on export of diesel and aviation turbine fuel (ATF) and slashed the levy to zero on petrol for the fortnight beginning October 31.

IOCL share price closed 0.12% lower at Rs.130 per share on BSE with a market capitalisation of Rs.1,83,576.10 crore on Friday, October 30. Higher diesel export duty can put pressure on export realisations from refining operations, whereas a cut on petrol export duty would bring some relief.

BPCL stock closed 1.47% lower at Rs.284.30 per share on BSE with an Mcap of Rs.1,23,342.68 crore on Friday. HPCL share price ended 0.72% lower at Rs.339.50 per share on BSE with an MCap of Rs.72,239.57 crore.

The government marginally hiked duty on ATF exports to Rs.11/litre from Rs.10.5/litre for the fortnight. The special additional excise duty (SAED) rate also increased on diesel exports. The SAED, along with road and infrastructure cess on export of diesel surged from Rs.8.5 per litre to Rs.11.5 per litre.

The duty on petrol exports was also slashed to nil by the government on Saturday. Petrol exports duty stood at Rs.2.5 per litre earlier. The recent changes on petrol duty came months after the government imposed export duty on diesel and ATF in March.

The windfall tax was levied on fuels to increase their domestic availability amid the war in West Asia. The move was also implemented to prevent exporters from taking undue advantage due to price differences as global crude oil prices saw sharp surge since the beginning of the West Asia war earlier this year.
